newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil publishes 1997/98 sugar crop plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil publishes 1997/98 sugar crop plan.

text.p: Brazilian 1997/98 sugar production should reach 13.48 million tonnes, of which 5.39 million will be available for exports, according to the government's crop plan published today in the official gazette.
Sugar production in the center-south is expected to reach 10.23 million tonnes with the remaining 3.25 million tonnes to come from the north/northeast region.
Exports will be 3.68 million tonnes from the center-south and 1.71 million from the north/northeast.
Total alcohol production is seen at 16.73 million cubic meters, of which 9.42 million will be hydrous alcohol.
The center-south should produce 5.07 million cubic meters anhydrous and 7.95 million cubic meters hydrous alcohol.
In the north/northeast, the corresponding figures are 1.22 million anhydrous and 1.48 million cubic meters hydrous alcohol.
Crushing in the center-south runs from May to November while in the north/northeast crushing is from September to April.
In the 1996/97 crop plan, total sugar output was put at 13.68 million tonnes, of which center-south production accounted for 10.47 million tonnes, and total exports 5.2 million.
The allocation for alcohol production in 1996/97 however was considerably lower at 13.89 million cubic meters.

The government had stated from the outset of talks on the 1997/98 crop plan that it wanted this year to use any increase in sugar cane production to boost alcohol output and eliminate the needs for imports. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
